newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Sugar export earnings support Mauritius rupee.
newsitem.headline: Sugar export earnings support Mauritius rupee.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee was firmer against the dollar but unchanged versus the pound on Thursday, reflecting international trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean commercial rate of 19.9555 to the dollar from 19.9935 on Wednesday, and at 33.553 for one pound, unchanged from Wednesday.

Forex dealers said the rupee's fixing followed the weakening trend of the dollar in overnight international markets: "If you look at the rupee against the French franc and German mark today, you will see its fixing was down (weaker) against these currencies as in trends in international markets," one said.
"Today, it's not the rupee up against all currencies as it was during the past couple of days after the central bank interventions," the dealer added.
This week, the central bank was seen supplying a total of 6.10 million dollars to commercial banks at prices lower than prevailing interbank rates on Monday and Tuesday.
Such central bank supply of dollars, coupled with the U.S. currency's weakening trend in international markets, supported the rupee, dealers said.
A further supply of hard currency to banks was seen on Wednesday with a Mauritius Sugar Syndicate tender sale of pounds obtained from sugar export proceeds.
"For the time being, commercial banks are not demanding (hard currency) from the interbank market. They can satisfy their customers' requirements," the dealer said.
